cards.explanation: The answer is that they're able to instruct one another. Paul says they're "…able to instruct one another." (Romans 15:14) He isn't just patting them on the head. He's saying the believers in Rome can teach each other. Friends, that's a compliment with some weight on it.

The answer is reminder. Paul calls it "…a bold reminder on some points…" (Romans 15:15) These folks already know a lot, so he isn't teaching from scratch. He's nudging them about things they've heard before. Friends, I've set a timer and still needed a reminder that the timer was going.

The answer is because of the grace God has given him. Paul says he wrote boldly "…because of the grace God has given me…" (Romans 15:15) His boldness isn't about his own importance. It rests on what God gave him. Now THAT is a confidence I can get behind.

The answer is offering. Paul says the goal is "…that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God…" (Romans 15:16) Gentiles are people from the nations who aren't Jewish. The offering is the people themselves, brought to God. That's a whole lot more meaningful than anything I've ever put in a cookie box.

The answer is True. Paul says the offering is "…sanctified by the Holy Spirit." (Romans 15:16) Sanctified means made holy. So the Spirit is the One doing that work, not Paul and not the people themselves.

The answer is only what Christ accomplished through him. Paul says, "I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me…" (Romans 15:18) He's thrilled, but he gives the credit where it belongs. That's the best kind of bragging, the kind that points somewhere else. I wish I could do that without stamping my own name on everything.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ." (Romans 15:19) That's a big stretch of ground. Friends, I'm tired just reading it.

The answer is where Christ was not known. Paul says, "…I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known…" (Romans 15:20) He wants to carry the news to people who haven't heard it. Friends, that's a goal worth lacing up your shoes for.

The answer is False. Paul quotes, "Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand." (Romans 15:21) So people who were never told will see and understand. Paul brings it in right after saying he aspired to preach where Christ was not known.
The answer is False. Paul says, "…there are no further opportunities for me in these regions…" (Romans 15:23) He has fully proclaimed the gospel there. That frees him to look toward the next place.
The answer is Spain. Paul writes, "I hope to see you on my way to Spain." (Romans 15:24) Rome is a stop along the way, not the final destination. Spain is a long way off, so he's thinking big.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey." (Romans 15:24) He plans to stop, enjoy their company and then be sent on his way. He's not just driving by.

The answer is the poor among the saints there. The contribution is "…for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem." (Romans 15:26) The saints are God's people, the believers. So this gift is headed straight to those in need among them. Simple, and kind.

The answer is material blessings. Paul says the Gentiles "…are obligated to minister to them with material blessings." (Romans 15:27) They shared in the spiritual blessings, so they give back in material ones. Material means real, practical things, like the gift Paul is carrying.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you." (Romans 15:28) So the delivery in Jerusalem comes first. After that he sets off for Spain by way of Rome.

The answer is True. Paul says, "I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ." (Romans 15:29) He is sure about it, and he doesn't hedge. That's a visit worth waiting for.

The answer is by praying to God for him. Paul asks them "…to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me." (Romans 15:30) Prayer is how they get in the fight with him, even from far away. You don't need a boat for that.

The answers are unbelievers for the first blank and acceptable for the second. Paul asks for prayer "…that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea…" (Romans 15:31) He knows there's danger and he asks his friends to pray about it. Honest and brave. He also asks "…that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there…" (Romans 15:31) He wants the gift to be received well by the believers in Jerusalem. I think that's a very human thing to hope for.
